YMM Encoding
The first source operand is a YMM register. The second source operand is a YMM register, a 256-bit
memory location, or a broadcast 64-bit memory location. The destination is a mask register.
ZMM Encoding
The first source operand is a ZMM register. The second source operand is a ZMM register, a 512-bit
memory location, or a broadcast 64-bit memory location. The destination is a mask register.
The EVEX encoded versions of this instruction write to the destination based on the supplied k mask
per 64-bit element and support memory fault suppression.

(V)CMPPD Immediate Operand Encoding
CMPPD uses only bits [2:0] of the 8-bit immediate operand and functions as if imm[4:3] are 00b.
VCMPPD uses bits [4:0] of the 8-bit immediate operand.
The following table shows the immediate operand value for (V)CMPPD and (V)CMPPS.Some
comparison operations that are not directly supported by immediate-byte encodings can be
implemented by swapping the contents of the source and destination operands and executing the
appropriate comparison of the swapped values. These additional comparison operations are shown
with the directly supported comparison operations. The “^” operator in the table, like the XOR
operator, toggles the value on the left if the value on the right is a ‘1’.

This extended-form instruction has 128-bit, 256-bit, and 512-bit encodings:
XMM Encoding
Converts four packed single-precision floating-point values in an XMM register to four packed 16-bit
floating-point values and writes the converted values to the low-order 64 bits of the destination XMM
register or to a 64-bit memory location. When the result is written to the destination XMM register,
the high-order 64 bits in the destination XMM register and the upper 128 bits of the corresponding
YMM register are cleared to 0s.
YMM Encoding
Converts eight packed single-precision floating-point values in a YMM register to eight packed 16-
bit floating-point values and writes the converted values to the low-order 128 bits of a YMM register
or to a 128-bit memory location. Bits [511:128] of the YMM register that corresponds to the
destination are cleared.
ZMM Encoding
Converts sixteen packed single-precision floating-point values in a ZMM register or a 512-bit
memory location to sixteen packed 16-bit floating-point values and writes the converted values to the
low-order 256 bits of a ZMM register or to a 256-bit memory location.
The EVEX encoded versions of this instruction write to the destination based on the supplied k mask
per 16-bit element and support memory fault suppression.
